analysis.title: GS Global Equities Call
key_insights: US futures are lower but calmer (SPX -25bps, NDX -15bps, RTY -55bps) as the tech/AI unwind stabilizes for now. DRAM is +2.5%, SMH +50bps pre-market, Hynix +4%, Samsung +40bps, Tokyo Electron flat.

AI vs SPX ex-AI had its worst relative day since the DeepSeek unwind. Breadth widened: over 300 SPX members closed green and over 60% of SPX members are above their 50dma, the highest share in two months.
GS HF Positioning Pair (GSTHVIPP) finished down about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% MTD.

Overnight micro headlines centered on high-bar prints that are for sale. BE (-2.5% pre-market) had a very strong quarter but investors are focused on cash conversion. WDC (-2%) had a beat and raise but incremental capex concerns weigh on the shares.

Macro overnight was light. WTI is up 1.75% at $101.25 and UST yields are 3-4bps higher across the curve. Japan's September national CPI was hot ahead of next week's BoJ meeting. Europe flash PMIs were mixed (France worse, Germany mixed, UK better).

Today's calendar: UMich consumer sentiment, US manufacturing PMI, Eurozone manufacturing and services PMIs, ECB CPI expectations, Japan CPI and manufacturing PMI, UK manufacturing PMI. Earnings pre-market: BAH, FCNCA, BCPC, AXP, SLB. Apple 'iPhone Duo' goes on sale.

Risk commentary: the index is breaking lower on heavyweights with extraordinary dispersion underneath. Equal weight/RSP closed near session highs, up 68bps. Popular longs fell mid-single digits while popular shorts were flat to higher, which the desk reads as a position flush that went well beyond fundamentals.

The desk lists concerns that are no longer being differentiated: ability to deliver gigawatts, too many gigawatts, insufficient capital, insufficient power, post-midterm politics and cybersecurity. Next week's hyperscaler results are seen as critical, especially backlog-to-revenue conversion, deployment pace and funding. The desk still sees frontier model development as robust.

The desk expected Korea to fall another mid-single digits this morning. The absence of another air pocket is read as encouraging. The desk says the baby has been thrown out with the bathwater across electricals, aerospace and transport, and that at these levels the market is pricing fairly extreme outcomes.

Momentum: the GS High Beta Momentum Pair (GSPRHIMO) has erased all YTD gains after a 43% drawdown (it was up about 70% at its June peak) and is back at September lows. Past winners are underperforming in a broad AI/semis selloff as the cost-versus-returns debate was reinforced by META earnings. This is the worst day for AI Beneficiaries (GSTMTAIP) vs Top 500 ex AI (SPXXAI) since DeepSeek Monday.

The desk continues to like the broadening trade. SPXXAI has outperformed SPX by 6pp in October. AI is about 50% of SPX and 45% of SPX names have negative beta to the index. Buying dips in the momentum factor has historically worked, and the desk favors limited-loss structures for clients wanting to buy the factor.

GS research on AI labor displacement: each 1% rise in labor productivity from technology temporarily lifts unemployment by 0.3-0.4pp at peak, fading after two years. Under a 15% AI productivity increase, about 9% of workers could be temporarily displaced. Job losses drive displacement more than slower hiring, so AI layoffs should be a good real-time guide, and industry and occupation analyses point to upside risk to labor disruption.

Prime book: more than two-thirds of hedge funds finished down and concentrated shorts squeezed further in the second half. For the first time since COVID, all three broad equity strategies fell more than 1% on the same day. Global Fundamental L/S was -1.4% (-2.1 SD), the worst day since July 16, -3.8% MTD and +8.8% YTD. TMT funds were -2.7%, -9.6% MTD and +8.0% YTD. Systematic L/S was -1.3% (-3.4 SD), the third-worst day since December 2023, +19.0% YTD. Multi-strats were -1.9% (-3.2 SD), the second-worst day since the April 2025 tariff sell-off.

Flows: no sign of buying the AI theme on the desk's flow yesterday and little rotation into defensives. The floor finished 9.6% better for sale, asset managers about 20% better for sale (large cap tech and ETFs), and hedge funds 10% better for sale (semis and hardware, plus ETF shorting with shorts outpacing long sales 2:1). Activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale.

Chart of the day: the SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over the last 9 sessions since 10/12, the biggest 9-day underperformance in 20+ years. The SOX is testing its 200-day average for the first time since June 2025 (Callahan).

tension_points.bull_case: GS likes the broadening trade: SPXXAI outperformed SPX by 6pp in October, over 60% of SPX members are above their 50dma, and buying dips in momentum has historically worked with cleaner positioning.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI/semis selloff is deepening: the SOX is down 13% vs the S&P in 9 sessions, GSPRHIMO is back at September lows, and the META print reinforced concerns about AI costs versus returns. Flows show no buying of the AI theme.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's major hyperscaler results, specifically how backlog converts to revenue, deployment pace and funding commentary.
